quizzes.title: Key terms across the lectures
quizzes.intro: Mill words used in spinning and weaving costing.

questions.q: OPS, the usual measure of ring-frame production, stands for
questions.explain: Production is quoted as ounces made by one spindle in one shift; it falls as the count gets finer.

questions.q: In spinning, “yield” means
options: The share of cotton that becomes yarn
questions.explain: A yield of 82% means 100 lb of cotton gives 82 lb of yarn; the rest is waste.

questions.q: In combed-yarn costing, noil is
options: The short fibre removed in combing
questions.explain: Combing removes short fibres as noil, which sells for much more than ordinary waste.

questions.q: In these lectures one bag of yarn weighs
questions.explain: Yarn is costed and sold in bags of 100 lb.

questions.q: B-grade fabric is
options: Fabric with faults, sold at a lower price
questions.explain: Faulty fabric still used yarn and loom time, but brings in less money.

questions.q: Warp contraction (crimp) is allowed for in costing because
options: Warp yarn is cheaper than weft
The yarn in the cloth is longer than the cloth itself
The loom runs slower than its rated speed
questions.explain: Yarn bends over the crossing threads, so one metre of cloth contains more than one metre of each warp end.

questions.q: A finer count has a higher OPS than a coarse count.
questions.explain: Finer yarn is lighter per unit length, so each spindle makes fewer ounces per shift.

questions.q: FCL in export costing means
questions.explain: A full container load is one whole container used for one shipment.

questions.q: In the yarn-mix decision, the “scarce resource” of the spinning mill is
questions.explain: There are only 46 frames, so the question is which count earns most from each frame.

questions.q: Export charges that are fixed per container become smaller per metre when more metres fit in the container.
questions.explain: The same container charge is divided by more metres, so a lighter fabric carries less export cost per metre.

quizzes.title: Linking the ideas
quizzes.intro: How production figures and prices combine into contribution per frame and per loom.

questions.q: Bags per frame per day are found from
questions.explain: Ounces per spindle per shift × spindles × shifts gives ounces a day; ÷ 16 gives lb and ÷ 100 gives bags.

questions.q: Cotton cost per lb of yarn, before any waste credit, is
questions.explain: More than 1 lb of cotton is needed for 1 lb of yarn, so the cost is divided by the yield.

questions.q: Count A earns Rs 900 per bag and makes 25 bags per frame a day. Count B earns Rs 1,700 per bag and makes 9 bags. Which earns more per frame?
options: B, because its contribution per bag is higher
questions.explain: Per frame: A = 900 × 25 = 22,500; B = 1,700 × 9 = 15,300. Contribution per bag alone is misleading.

questions.q: Why can a mill not simply put every frame on the count with the highest contribution per frame?
options: Because another limit, such as daily shipment of bags, may be reached first
Because the dollar price would change
questions.explain: In the lecture the 780-bag shipping limit stops the mill from running all 46 frames on coarse counts.

questions.q: Warp weight per yard of fabric is
questions.explain: Each end is one yard plus allowances long, and 840 × Ne yards weigh one pound.

questions.q: If loom efficiency rises from 85% to 90% with everything else unchanged, the contribution per loom per day
options: Rises, because more metres are woven
questions.explain: Contribution per metre is the same, but the loom makes more metres in the day.

questions.q: A higher picks per inch, at the same rpm, makes the loom produce
questions.explain: Each inch of cloth needs more picks, so the same number of picks per minute gives less length.

questions.q: Commission that is a percentage of sale proceeds is a variable cost of the order.
questions.explain: It arises only because the order is sold and rises with the sale value.

questions.q: The dollar price of an export fabric falls by one cent when the exchange rate is Rs 60. Proceeds per metre fall by
questions.explain: US$ 0.01 × 60 = Rs 0.60 per metre, a noticeable slice of a margin of about Rs 12.

questions.q: The yarn in B-grade fabric must still be paid for, so yarn cost per metre of good fabric is grossed up for the B-grade percentage.
questions.explain: Dividing by (1 − B-grade) charges the good metres with the yarn consumed by the faulty ones.

quizzes.title: Mixed calculations
quizzes.intro: Production and cost calculations for spinning and weaving with new figures.

questions.q: A ring frame has 480 spindles and runs three shifts. At 1 OPS, how many ounces does it make in a day?
questions.explain: 480 spindles × 3 shifts × 1 oz = 1,440 oz, which is 0.9 bags of 100 lb.

questions.q: A frame makes 0.9 bags a day at 1 OPS. How many bags a day does it make on a count that runs at 17 OPS? Answer to one decimal.
questions.explain: 0.9 × 17 = 15.3 bags a day.

questions.q: Cotton costs Rs 36 per lb and the yield is 80%. What is the cotton cost per lb of yarn, before any credit for waste?
questions.explain: 36 ÷ 0.80 = Rs 45 per lb of yarn.

questions.q: Yarn sells at US$ 2.20 per kg and the dollar is Rs 60. Taking a 100 lb bag as 45.36 kg, what is the price per bag in rupees, to the nearest rupee?
questions.explain: 2.20 × 60 = Rs 132 per kg; × 45.36 kg = Rs 5,988 per bag.

questions.q: A bag sells for Rs 5,900 and its variable cost (cotton, packing and export charges) is Rs 4,700. A frame makes 9.3 bags a day. What is the contribution per frame per day?
A fabric has 3,600 warp ends of Ne 20. Allowing 10% for contraction, what is the warp weight per yard of fabric in lb, to three decimals?
A loom runs at 600 rpm at 85% efficiency, inserting 51 picks per inch. How many inches of fabric does it make per minute?
questions.explain: 600 × 0.85 ÷ 51 = 10 inches a minute.

questions.q: A loom makes 10 inches of fabric a minute. How many yards does it make in 24 hours?
questions.explain: 10 × 1,440 minutes ÷ 36 = 400 yards a day.

questions.q: A 40 ft container carries 57,000 lb. A fabric weighs 0.60 lb per metre. How many metres fit in the container?
Sale proceeds are Rs 44.00 a metre and total variable cost Rs 32.50 a metre. A loom makes 440 m a day. What is the contribution per loom per day?

quizzes.title: Case study
quizzes.intro: One export order followed from yarn cost to the profit of a loom.

questions.q: What is the yarn cost per metre of fabric?
questions.explain: Rs 56 per lb × 0.50 lb = Rs 28 per metre.

questions.q: How many metres fit in one container?
questions.explain: 57,000 lb ÷ 0.50 lb per metre = 114,000 metres.

questions.q: What are the export charges per metre, in rupees to two decimals?
What are the sale proceeds per metre in rupees?
What is the commission per metre, in rupees to two decimals?
What is the total variable cost per metre (yarn, sizing and packing, export charges and commission), to two decimals?
What is the contribution per metre, to two decimals?
How many yards does one loom weave in a day?
Taking the loom’s production as 494 metres a day, what is its contribution per day, to the nearest rupee?
With a contribution of about Rs 6,694 a day and a fixed cost of Rs 4,000, the loom
questions.explain: Profit per loom = contribution − fixed cost = 6,694 − 4,000 ≈ Rs 2,700 a day.

quizzes.case: A mill weaves a grey fabric that contains 0.50 lb of yarn per metre. Yarn costs Rs 560 per 10 lb. Sizing and packing cost Rs 2.00 per metre. The fabric is exported at US$ 0.75 per metre with the dollar at Rs 60. A 40 ft container carries 57,000 lb of fabric; export charges are Rs 114,000 per container and commission is 1% of the sale proceeds. Each loom runs at 750 rpm with 50 picks per inch at 90% efficiency for 24 hours, and has a fixed cost of Rs 4,000 a day.

quizzes.title: Group challenge
quizzes.intro: Decisions and two-step calculations across spinning and weaving.

questions.q: Cotton is bought at Rs 2,800 per maund of 37.34 kg. Taking 1 kg = 2.2046 lb, what is the cotton cost per lb, to two decimals?
Cotton costs Rs 34 per lb. Yield is 82%, and the 18% waste is sold at 15% of the cotton price. What is the adjusted cotton cost per lb of yarn, to two decimals?
questions.explain: 34 ÷ 0.82 = 41.46; waste per lb of yarn = 0.18 ÷ 0.82 lb worth 34 × 0.15 each = 1.12; net Rs 40.34.

questions.q: A frame costs Rs 14,000 a day to own and run. It makes 9.27 bags a day of Ne 20, whose variable cost is Rs 4,330 a bag. What price per bag makes the frame break even, to the nearest rupee?
questions.explain: Variable cost 4,330 + fixed 14,000 ÷ 9.27 = Rs 5,840 per bag.

questions.q: A mill has 46 frames and can ship 780 bags a day. Count X makes 20 bags per frame and earns Rs 23,000 per frame; count Y makes 9 bags per frame and earns Rs 16,000. Putting all frames on X would
options: Break the shipping limit, since 46 × 20 = 920 bags
Earn less than putting all on Y
questions.explain: 920 bags exceed the 780 that can be shipped, so some frames must move to the count that uses fewer bags per frame.

questions.q: In that mill (46 frames, 780 bags a day; X = 20 bags per frame, Y = 9 bags per frame), how many frames should run X if all 46 frames are used and exactly 780 bags are made? Answer to one decimal.
questions.explain: Let x frames run X: 20x + 9(46 − x) = 780, so x = (780 − 414) ÷ 11 = 33.3 frames.

questions.q: A fabric has 0.26 lb of warp at Rs 55 per lb and 0.25 lb of weft at Rs 50 per lb in each yard. What is the yarn cost per metre, to two decimals? (1 metre = 1.0936 yards)
A loom weaves 480 yards a day, of which 1% is B-grade. How many metres of A-grade does it make? Answer to one decimal. (1 yard = 0.9144 m)
A buyer offers a price that gives a contribution of Rs 3,600 per loom per day. The loom’s fixed cost is Rs 4,000 a day and there is no other work for it. In the short run the mill should
options: Refuse, because the order makes a loss
Accept, because Rs 3,600 of the fixed cost is recovered instead of nothing
Accept only if the price is doubled
questions.explain: Fixed cost is paid anyway. A positive contribution reduces the loss, so the order is better than an idle loom.

questions.q: Two fabrics with the same price per metre always give the same contribution per loom per day.
questions.explain: Contribution per loom depends also on the variable cost per metre and on how many metres the loom makes, which changes with picks per inch.

questions.q: Export charges are Rs 120,000 per 40 ft container (57,000 lb). How much lower, in rupees per metre to two decimals, are they for a fabric of 0.40 lb per metre than for one of 0.60 lb per metre?
